- When sentiment drops to 0.00 or negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward momentum dampening.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model overestimates mean; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., <0.5) over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
- Model often overfits recent history (e.g., 30d forecast follows 18d trend), but true outcome shows longer-term volatility; reduce forecast smoothness or add volatility buffer.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30d forecast mean, check sentiment for “reversal” signals (e.g., 0.00 → 0.40+); adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift.
- Forecasting horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment rises sharply, delay forecast adjustment until next 3–5 days.
